messages:
incident-bot: Pager: Elevated 5xx rate detected for Hosted API and Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 starting ~09:14 UTC. 5xx rate ~15% and p95 latency jumped to ~1.2s. Auto-alerts triggered.
lia: taking this. +1 oncall. switching channel to incident channel.
sanjay: seeing same in dashboards — ELB health checks failing intermittently, TLS handshakes timing out for internal controlplane -> auth svc calls.
maria: quick check: `curl -v https://eu-west-1-api.redwood.ai/health` returns `HTTP/1.1 503` and TLS handshake stalls on multiple hosts.
oliver: confirmed Dedicated pool instances in eu-west-1 report lots of `connect() timeout` and `tls: handshake failure` in nginx logs.
lia: suspected NLB/ELB edge issue or regional NAT gateway egress saturation. opening AWS console now, pinging support. @ops-oncall please start routing plan B.
ops-oncall: on it — shifting routing for new Hosted API traffic away from eu-west-1 to eu-west-2 and eu-central-1 for best-effort. Will update load-balancer routing rules and enable cross-region fallback. This will affect latency for EU customers but should reduce 5xx.
sanjay: will also scale up capacity in eu-west-2 Dedicated pools to absorb failover. Starting quick scale + increase reserved concurrency.
maria: posting AWS status link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incidents/ (opened support case: #1234567890).
lia: mitigation steps so far: 1) Implemented routing override to avoid primary NLBs in eu-west-1 for new requests. 2) Enabled TLS downgrade fallback (allow older ciphers) for a small subset to reduce handshake failures. 3) Warmed up Spare Dedicated nodes in eu-west-2. 4) Disabled some non-critical middleware (request-level tracing sampling) to lower connection overhead.
oliver: sample logs: ```
[09:16:02] nginx: SSL_do_handshake() failed (SSL: error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number)
[09:16:05] control-plane: dial tcp 10.2.3.4:443: connect: connection timed out
```
lia: customer impact: hosted API clients routing through eu-west-1 may see 5xx or elevated latency. Dedicated customers with pools pinned to eu-west-1 may experience degraded throughput or increased request errors until failover completes. Sending customer-comm draft to SRE comms channel.
ops-oncall: ETA for basic mitigation (routing + fallback) ~15-25m. Full restoration depends on AWS region fix; AWS support estimated investigation time 1-3 hours in case of regional NLB control-plane issue.
sanjay: temp mitigation notes for apps: set `region_preference=eu-central-1` or use `x-region-fallback: eu-west-2` header to force cross-region routing. Update SDK quickstart in status page.
maria: adding monitor adjustments: suppress noise alerts for spike while mitigation in progress, but keep pager on if 5xx > 10% after routing change.
lia: handoff: I'm IC. @sanjay you own routing changes and Dedicated scaling. @oliver you own log collection + evidence for AWS. @maria you manage customer comms and alerting. @ops-oncall keep AWS case updated.
aws-support-bot: AWS case #1234567890 updated by support engineer. They've identified degraded NLB TLS handshake rates in eu-west-1 affecting TCP connections to customer target groups and are investigating downstream control plane.
oliver: shared packet captures and handshake traces to AWS. They asked for SNI samples and examples which I uploaded.
lia: quick customer impact summary for pager: ~12% of Hosted API requests from EU routed through eu-west-1 returned 5xx over last 10m; several Dedicated pools showing increased error budgets. No data plane data loss detected. Estimated customer-visible downtime for pinned Dedicated pools if customer does not accept failover: degraded for 1-3 hours.
maria: posting to status page now (short): "We are investigating elevated errors and latency for EU (eu-west-1). We're routing traffic to alternate regions and scaling capacity; customer impact for some customers may persist while AWS investigates. Updates every 30m."
sanjay: routing change propagated to 85% of edge nodes. New requests should start avoiding affected NLBs.
ops-oncall: monitoring shows 5xx dropping to ~4% and p95 latency improving. Still seeing intermittent TLS handshake errors from a subset of controlplane hosts.
lia: good progress. keep AWS case open and escalate if situation reappears. I'll keep this channel updated; switching to incident update cadence (every 30m). :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident recorded: incident-2026-4923456789. Severity: Sev2. Updates scheduled every 30 minutes.
